His autem sic se habentibus, et in omnibus antiquis et probatissimis et veteribus scripturis numero hoc posito, et testimonium perhibentibus his, qui facie ad faciem Johannem viderunt, et ratione docente nos, quoniam numerus nominis bestiz secundum Greecorum computationem per literas quee in eo sunt, sexcentos — habebit, et sexaginta, et sex; hoc est, decadas sequales hecatontasin, et hecatontadas eequales monasin ; Numerus enim qui digitus sex, similiter custoditus, recapitulationes ostendit universee apostasize ejus que initio, et que in mediis temporibus, et quae in fine erit ; ignoro quomodo erraverunt quidam sequentes idiotismum, et medium frustrantes numerum nominis, quinquaginta numeros deducentes, pro sex decadis unam decadem volentes esse. [ Hoc autem arbitror scriptorum peccatum fuisse, ut solet fieri, quoniam et- per literas numeri ponuntur, facile literam Graecam, que Sexaginta enuntiat numerum, in iota Grecorum literam expansam ;]| post deinde quidam sine exquisitione hoc acceperunt; alii quidem simpliciter et idiotice usurpaverunt denarium numerum : quidam autem per ignorantiam ausi sunt et nomina exquirere, habentia falsum erroris numerum. Sed his quidem qui simpliciter et malitia hoe fecerunt, arbitramur veniam daria Deo. Quotquot autem secundum inanem gloriam statuunt nomina continentia falsum numerum, et quod a se fuerit adinventum nomen, definierunt esse illius qui venturus est; non sine damno tales exient, quippe qui et semetipsos, et credentes sibi seduxerunt. Et priquidem damnum est excidere a veritate, et quod non sit, quasi arbitrari: post deinde, apponenti vel auferenti de Scriptura peenam non modicam fore, in quam incidere necesse est eum qui sit talis, Subsequetur autem et aliud non quodlibet periculum eos, qui falso preesumunt scire nomen ejus. Si enim aliud quidem thi putant, aliud autem ille habens adveniet, facile seducentur ab eo, quasi necdum adsit ille, quem cavere convenit. 2. Oportet itaque tales discere, et ad yerum recurrere nominis numerum; ut non in pseudoprophetarum loco deputentur. Sed scientes firmum numerum qui a Scriptura annuntiatus est, id est, sexcentorum sexaginta sex, sustineant primum quidem divisionem regni in decem: post deinde illis regnantibus, et incipientibus corrigere sua negotia, et augere suum regnum, qui de improyiso advenerit regnum sibi vindicans, et terrebit praedietos, habens nomen continens preedictum numerum, hune vere cognoscere esse abominationem desolationis. Cum autem ®yastaverit Antichristus hic omnia in hoe mundo, regnabit annis tribus et mensibus sex, et sedebit in templo Hierosolymis ; tune veniet Dominus de ccelis in nubibus, in gloria Patris, illum quidem, et obedientes ei in stagnum ignis mittens; adducens autem justis regni tempora, hoc est requietionem, septimam diem sanctificatam ; et restituens Abrahz promissionem heereditatis : in quo regno ait Dominus, multos ab oriente et occidente venientes, recumbere cum Abraham, Isaac, et Jacob.
thought_title: The Number of the Beast's Name
pass_a_gloss: These things being so, and the number being established in all ancient and approved and old scriptures, and the testimony being borne by those who saw John face to face, and reason teaching us that the number of the name of the beast, according to the computation of the Greeks through the letters which are in it, will have six hundred and sixty-six, that is, equal tens of hundreds and equal hundreds of units; for the number which is six, similarly preserved, shows the recapitulations of his apostasy, which was from the beginning, and which is in the middle times, and which will be in the end; I do not know how some have erred, following foolishness, and frustrating the middle of the number of the name, deducing fifty numbers, wishing one decade to be instead of six decades; but I think this was a sin of the scribes, as often happens, because they also put numbers through letters, easily changing the Greek letter which announces the number sixty into the Greek letter iota; then some accepted this without investigation; others indeed used the number ten simply and foolishly; some, however, dared to investigate names, having the false number of error; but to those who did this simply and with malice, we think pardon will be given by God; however, as many as establish names containing the false number, and define the invented name to be that of the one who will come, will not go out without loss, since they have deceived themselves and those who believe them; and indeed the loss is to fall away from the truth, and to think that which is not; then, adding to or taking away from Scripture will result in no small penalty, which it is necessary for such a person to incur; but another danger, not insignificant, will also follow those who falsely presume to know his name; for if they think one thing, but he comes with another, they will easily be seduced by him, as if he were not yet present, whom it is fitting to beware of; therefore, it is necessary for such people to learn and return to the truth of the number of the name, so that they may not be considered pseudo-prophets; but knowing the firm number announced by Scripture, that is, six hundred sixty-six, let them first endure the division of the kingdom into ten; then, with those reigning and beginning to correct their affairs and increase their kingdom, the one who will come unexpectedly, claiming the kingdom for himself, and terrifying the aforementioned, having the name containing the aforementioned number, let them truly recognize him to be the abomination of desolation; and the Apostle says: when they will say, Peace and security, then sudden destruction will come upon them; and indeed, not only his sudden coming, but also the tribe of six, by which he will come, is revealed, saying: the voice of the neighing of his horses will move the whole earth; and he will come and devour the earth and its fullness and the city and those who dwell in it; and because of this, this tribe is not counted among those who are saved in the Apocalypse; therefore, it is more certain and without danger to endure the fulfillment of prophecy than to suspect and divine any names; since many names can be found having the aforementioned number, and nevertheless, the same question will remain; for if many names are found having this number, which he who comes will bear, it is asked; because we say these things not because of a lack of names having the number of his name, but because of fear and zeal for the truth; for the name Euanthas has the number in question, but we affirm nothing about it; the name has the number six hundred sixty-six; and it is very likely, since this last kingdom has this name; for the Latins are those who now reign; but we do not glory in this; and also Titan, written with two Greek vowels e and «, has the predicted number in itself, and is worthy of faith; and the number of its letters is six, with single syllables consisting of three letters, and is old and removed; for none of the kings who are according to us have been called Titan, nor do the idols which are publicly worshiped among the Greeks and barbarians have this name; and this name is considered divine by many, so that even the sun is called Titan by those who now hold it; and it contains a certain show of vengeance and revenge, since he pretends to avenge those who have been mistreated; and this name is also ancient, and worthy of faith, and royal, but more tyrannical; therefore, since this name Titan has so much persuasion, and so much verisimilitude, that we gather from many things that perhaps Titan will be the name of the one who comes, we nevertheless will not risk it, nor will we assertively pronounce that he will have this name; knowing that if it were necessary to proclaim his name openly at the present time, it would have been published by him who also saw the Apocalypse; for it was not seen long before, but almost in our own century, at the end of Domitian's reign; now, however, the number of the name shows that we should beware of the one who is coming, knowing who he is; but the name itself is silent, because it is not worthy to be proclaimed by the Holy Spirit; for if it had been proclaimed by him, perhaps it would have remained for a long time; but now, since it is not, and will ascend from the abyss, and will go into perdition, as if it were not; thus, neither is his name proclaimed; for the name of that which is not is not proclaimed; when, however, the Antichrist will have established all things in this world, he will reign for three years and six months, and will sit in the temple of Jerusalem; then the Lord will come from heaven in the clouds, in the glory of the Father, sending him, and those who obey him, into the lake of fire; but bringing the times of the kingdom to the just, that is, rest, sanctifying the seventh day; and restoring the promise of inheritance to Abraham; in which kingdom the Lord says that many will come from the east and the west, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
pass_b_english: All these facts are confirmed by every ancient, approved, and authoritative Scripture, and by the testimony of those who saw John face to face; reason itself also teaches that the number of the beast's name, calculated according to the Greek method through the letters that compose it, comes to six hundred sixty-six—that is, equal tens of hundreds and equal hundreds of units. The digit six, similarly preserved, displays the recapitulations of his apostasy: the one that began at the start, the one in the middle times, and the one that will occur at the end. I cannot understand how certain persons went astray by following a foolish error, mutilating the middle of the number of the name by subtracting fifty so that they could make a single decade stand for six decades. I judge this to have been a scribal sin, as often happens, because numbers are also expressed by letters, and the Greek letter that signifies sixty was easily expanded into the Greek iota. Afterward some accepted this without investigation; others simply and foolishly used the number ten; still others dared to search out names that contained the false number of error. To those who acted merely out of simplicity and without malice we believe God will grant pardon. But as for those who, for the sake of empty glory, establish names containing the false number and declare their own invented name to be that of the coming one—they will not escape loss, because they have deceived both themselves and those who believe them. The loss itself is to fall away from the truth and to treat what does not exist as real. Moreover, adding to or taking away from Scripture brings no small penalty, which such a person must inevitably incur. Another danger, by no means slight, will also follow those who falsely presume to know his name: if they think one thing while he arrives with another, they will easily be seduced by him, as though he were not yet present—the very one we ought to beware of.

Therefore such people must learn and return to the true number of the name, lest they be classed as false prophets. Knowing the firm number announced by Scripture—six hundred sixty-six—let them first endure the division of the kingdom into ten. Then, while those ten reign and begin to set their affairs in order and expand their dominion, the one who comes unexpectedly and claims the kingdom for himself will terrify those former rulers; having a name that contains the aforesaid number, he must be recognized as the abomination of desolation. The Apostle also says: when they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them. Not only his sudden coming, but also the tribe of six by which he will come, is revealed: "The voice of the neighing of his horses will shake the whole earth; he will come and devour the earth and its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it." Because of this, that tribe is not counted among the saved in the Apocalypse. It is therefore more certain and without danger to await the fulfillment of prophecy than to speculate and guess at any names; for many names can be found that possess the predicted number, and yet the same question would remain. If many names are discovered bearing this number—the one the coming one will bear—it will still be asked which one is his.

We say these things not because of a shortage of names that have the number of his name, but out of reverence and zeal for the truth. The name Euanthas possesses the number in question, yet we affirm nothing about it. The name itself totals six hundred sixty-six, and it is very plausible, since this final kingdom bears that name; the Latins are the ones who now reign, but we do not boast in this. Also the name Titan, written with two Greek vowels e and i, contains the predicted number in itself and is worthy of confidence. It consists of six letters, with single syllables made of three letters each, and it is ancient and set apart; for none of the kings who belong to us has been called Titan, nor do the idols publicly worshiped among Greeks and barbarians bear that name. Many regard the name as divine, so that even the sun is called Titan by those who now hold power. The name also carries a certain display of vengeance and retribution, since he pretends to avenge those who have been mistreated. It is likewise ancient, trustworthy, and royal—yet more tyrannical. Because the name Titan carries such weight of persuasion and verisimilitude, we gather from many indications that perhaps the coming one will be called Titan; nevertheless we will not risk it, nor will we assertively pronounce that he will bear this name. We know that if it had been necessary to proclaim his name openly at the present time, it would have been published by the one who also saw the Apocalypse; for the vision was not seen long ago, but almost in our own century, at the end of Domitian's reign.

Now the number of the name is shown so that we may beware of the one who is coming, knowing who he is; but the name itself is kept silent, because it is not worthy to be proclaimed by the Holy Spirit. If it had been proclaimed by Him, perhaps it would have endured for a long time. But now, since the beast is not, yet will ascend from the abyss and go to perdition as though he did not exist, neither is his name proclaimed; for the name of that which is not is not proclaimed. When the Antichrist has established all things in this world, he will reign for three years and six months and will sit in the temple at Jerusalem. Then the Lord will come from heaven in clouds, in the glory of the Father, sending him and those who obey him into the lake of fire, but bringing the times of the kingdom to the just—that is, rest, sanctifying the seventh day—and restoring the promise of inheritance to Abraham. In that kingdom the Lord says many will come from east and west and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text, preserving the complex theological arguments regarding the number of the beast, the name Titan, and the eschatological timeline. All clauses in Pass A and B correspond to the Locked Latin. Scripture allusions (e.g., 'Peace and security', 'voice of the neighing of his horses') are handled correctly as part of the text flow without requiring external verse numbering that wasn't in the source, though the translator correctly identifies them as the Apostle's words.
